definitions.title: Green's Theorem (Circulation-Curl Form)
definitions.latex: \oint_C M \, dx + N \, dy = \iint_R \left( \frac{\partial N}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial M}{\partial y} \right) dA
definitions.statement: Let C be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane enclosing region R. The counterclockwise circulation around boundary C equals the double integral of the 2D scalar curl over R.
conditions: M and N have continuous partials on open set containing R
definitions.explanation: Microscopic rotations (curl) inside the region cancel on internal shared boundaries, leaving only the macroscopic boundary circulation.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Transforms boundary line integrals into planar double integrals.

definitions.title: Green's Theorem (Flux-Divergence Form)
definitions.latex: \oint_C M \, dy - N \, dx = \iint_R \left( \frac{\partial M}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial N}{\partial y} \right) dA = \iint_R \text{div}\,\mathbf{F} \, dA
definitions.statement: The total outward flux of F across boundary curve C equals the double integral of the divergence of F over region R.
conditions: Simple closed curve C enclosing region R
definitions.explanation: Microscopic sources and sinks inside R accumulate to produce net outward flux across the perimeter.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Planar version of the Divergence Theorem.
